title: Where Can I See Kakobuy QC Photos?
meta: Learn when Kakobuy QC photos become relevant, where to check the current item record, and how to separate warehouse images from listing photos.
targetKeyword: where to see Kakobuy QC photos
quickAnswer: Kakobuy's public information says quality checking becomes relevant after a product reaches its warehouse. To find photos for your item, inspect its current item, order, or warehouse record after that stage and look for the image area connected to the exact item. Public pages do not show a dependable universal menu path, so use the current interface or Kakobuy support if the photo section is unclear.
body:
## Quick Answer

Kakobuy's public information says quality checking becomes relevant after a product reaches its warehouse. To find photos for your item, inspect its current item, order, or warehouse record after that stage and look for the image area connected to the exact item. Public pages do not show a dependable universal menu path, so use the current interface or Kakobuy support if the photo section is unclear.

## First Confirm Which Photos You Need

Not every product image is a Kakobuy QC photo. The difference matters because each image type answers a different question.

Seller listing photos present the product before a specific item reaches a warehouse. They may show available colors, styles, size labels, or design details. They are useful for identifying the intended product, but they do not document the condition of a particular item.

Product research pages can organize listing photos beside a price reference, SKU choices, size data, and a source link. This gives you context before you rely on a marketplace record. These images still should not be treated as warehouse-issued QC photos unless their source is clearly identified.

Warehouse QC photos should be tied to a particular received item. They are useful only when you can match the image set to the item record, option, and stage you are reviewing.

## When Kakobuy QC Photos Become Relevant

Kakobuy's current public quality-inspection page states that quality checking is provided after products arrive at its warehouse. That establishes the relevant stage, but it does not prove one fixed menu path for every account or item.

Before looking for warehouse images, check the current status shown on your item record. If the item has not reached the stage described by Kakobuy, a warehouse image set may not yet be relevant. Do not use a community screenshot or an old tutorial to override the status displayed in your own account.

Interface labels can change. Start from the exact item record rather than a general gallery. Look for an image area, inspection section, or photo entry connected to that record. If the record is at the expected stage but no photo area is visible, use Kakobuy's current support channel and provide the item reference.

## Match the Photos to the Correct Item

A useful image set needs a clear identity. Compare the product title, source URL, item number, selected style, color, and size with the item you are checking.

Use this order:

1. Open the exact item record in your current account.
2. Confirm the product title or source identifier.
3. Compare the selected color, style, or size.
4. Check whether the images are attached to that same record.
5. Note any missing label, angle, or measurement as unknown.

Similar product names are not enough. A spreadsheet row, social post, or gallery may show another variation or another user's item. The images can still help you learn what to inspect, but they cannot document your own item without a matching record.

## What to Check in the Image Set

Begin with the whole product. Check whether the general shape, color placement, and main parts match the option shown on the item record.

Then inspect the details that matter for that product type. For shoes, that may include the toe, heel, both sides, outsole, interior size label, and visible stitching. For clothing, check the front, back, print placement, seams, tags, and any visible measurement reference. For bags, look at the exterior, base, corners, straps, closures, and interior when shown.

Record observations in plain language:

- The size label is readable.
- The heel is not shown clearly.
- The left side has a visible mark.
- The color looks different under the available lighting.
- No measurement reference appears in the set.

Avoid turning an image into a claim it cannot support. A photo may show a surface detail, but it cannot prove material composition, long-term wear, comfort, or authenticity.

## Compare Against the Source Record

Use the marketplace source record as a reference point. Compare its title, option labels, listed price, seller images, and item identifier with the record and photos you are reviewing.

This comparison can reveal a mismatch between the selected option and the photographed item. It can also show that the source page has changed since a spreadsheet or saved link was created.

The source record is time-sensitive. A working page does not establish that every old option, price, or photo is still current. Save the item identifier and review the live source before relying on a copied label.

## Product Research Before the Warehouse Stage

You can reduce confusion by recording the intended product before warehouse QC becomes relevant. The [CuriCart Kakobuy product research guide](https://www.curicart.com/en/agentsView_15_6.html) brings product images together with price references, selectable SKUs, size or style data, and available Weidian sources.

Three current examples provide different visual records:

- [THE ROGER Clubhouse Pro Tennis Shoes - Style 30](https://www.curicart.com/en/productview_4234_80.html?proname=on-the-roger-clubhouse-pro-tennis-shoes) shows several product photos, a listed-price reference, style choices, size labels, and a Weidian source record.
- [On Cloudmonster 1 White Gray - Style 21](https://www.curicart.com/en/productview_4203_79.html?proname=on-cloudmonster-1-running-shoes) provides multiple product views, a listed-price reference, and a detailed size list.
- [Nike Mind 001 Flyknit QS Slides - Style 16](https://www.curicart.com/en/productview_4160_77.html?proname=nike-slides-sandals) displays several images, selectable styles, shoe-size mappings, a reference price, and its Weidian source record.

Use these pages to practise identifying product photos, options, and source context. Do not treat their images as the warehouse QC record for an item in your Kakobuy account.

## What to Do When Photos Are Missing

First, confirm that you are viewing the correct item and the current status. Then refresh the record and check whether the image area is attached to another visible section of the same item page.

Next, compare the item number and selected option. A mismatch can make the available photos irrelevant even when images are present.

If the expected section remains absent, collect a short evidence set before contacting support:

- Item or record identifier.
- Current status shown on the page.
- Screenshot of the item record.
- The source URL.
- The specific photo or angle you cannot find.

Do not assume that another user's screenshot proves what your interface should show. Account state, item state, and interface updates may differ.

## What QC Photos Can and Cannot Tell You

QC photos can support a visual comparison. They may show whether a visible label, color, shape, size mark, surface, or included part appears consistent with the selected record.

They cannot reveal every hidden area. They also cannot confirm fit, comfort, internal construction, long-term durability, or authenticity. Lighting, camera angle, compression, and screen settings can change how color and texture appear.

Treat each image as a limited record. A good review ends with two lists: what the photos show and what remains unknown.

faq.question: Where can I see Kakobuy QC photos?
faq.answer: Check the current item, order, or warehouse record connected to the product after it reaches the quality-check stage. Kakobuy's public page confirms that quality checking follows warehouse arrival, but a universal public menu path was not verified. Use the live interface or current support if the image area is unclear.

faq.question: Are seller photos the same as Kakobuy QC photos?
faq.answer: No. Seller photos present a listing. Warehouse QC photos should relate to a specific received item. Compare the image source and item record before treating a photo as QC evidence.

faq.question: Why might I not see photos yet?
faq.answer: The visible item status, record selection, or current interface may explain the absence, but the exact reason cannot be confirmed without your live record. Check the item identifier and status before contacting support.

faq.question: What details should I check first?
faq.answer: Confirm the item, selected style, color, and size. Then review the whole product, labels, key surfaces, visible construction details, and any measurement reference relevant to the category.

faq.question: Can QC photos prove product authenticity?
faq.answer: No. Images can support visual observations, but they cannot establish authenticity, hidden construction, long-term durability, or a perfect fit.

title: Why Is My Kakobuy Product Link Not Working?
meta: Diagnose a Kakobuy product link that does not load. Check the full source URL, item identifier, live source page, options, and current error message.
quickAnswer: When a Kakobuy product link is not working, test the complete marketplace source URL first. Confirm that it begins with `http://` or `https://`, contains the expected item identifier, and opens at its original destination. Then compare Kakobuy's current error message with the live source page. Do not assume one cause: an incomplete URL, changed source record, temporary error, or unsupported page can look similar.
body:
## Quick Answer

When a Kakobuy product link is not working, test the complete marketplace source URL first. Confirm that it begins with `http://` or `https://`, contains the expected item identifier, and opens at its original destination. Then compare Kakobuy's current error message with the live source page. Do not assume one cause: an incomplete URL, changed source record, temporary error, or unsupported page can look similar.

## Start With the Exact Error You Can See

Write down the message before changing the link. The wording is evidence. A blank page, a network error, a “product may not exist” notice, and an incorrect product result are different problems.

A current Kakobuy item page can display the message: “This product may not exist. Please visit the above link to confirm.” The same interface tells the user to check the original link and offers a reload or manual fill-in path when that original link is valid.

That message does not prove the source item was deleted. It tells you to verify the source before deciding what happened.

Capture these details:

- The complete URL you entered.
- The marketplace domain.
- The visible item identifier.
- The exact Kakobuy message.
- The date and time of the check.
- Whether the original source page opens separately.

## Check Whether the URL Is Complete

Kakobuy's current manual product form asks for a product link that starts with `http://` or `https://`. A copied product name, shortened label, screenshot, or partial path is not the same as a complete URL.

Paste the link into a plain text field and inspect it. It should contain the scheme, domain, path, and product identifier needed by the source page. For a Weidian item, the numeric `itemID` is an important reference. Preserve the full URL until you know which parameters are optional.

Avoid copying a link from a visually shortened message. The displayed text may hide part of the destination. Use the browser's copy-link function when possible, then compare the pasted value with the address shown after the source page opens.

## Open the Original Source Separately

Test the marketplace URL outside the Kakobuy result page. This separates a source-page problem from a Kakobuy reading problem.

Record what happens:

1. The source page opens and shows the expected item.
2. The source opens but shows a different item or option.
3. The source redirects to a login, verification, or regional page.
4. The source returns an error or removed-item notice.
5. The source page loads only partly.

Do not treat all five outcomes as “dead link.” If the source opens correctly while Kakobuy shows an error, save both records and use Kakobuy's current reload, manual-entry, or support options. If the source itself no longer presents the item, an old spreadsheet label cannot restore it.

## Match the Item Identifier

Product titles are weak identifiers. Sellers and spreadsheet editors may use short names, translated names, or labels shared by several products.

For Weidian, find `itemID=` in the source URL and record the following digits. Compare them character by character. One changed digit points to a different source record.

Three current CuriCart examples show why this matters:

- [THE ROGER Style 30 record](https://www.curicart.com/en/productview_4234_80.html?proname=on-the-roger-clubhouse-pro-tennis-shoes) points to Weidian itemID `7805795543`.
- [Cloudmonster Style 21 record](https://www.curicart.com/en/productview_4203_79.html?proname=on-cloudmonster-1-running-shoes) points to Weidian itemID `7808777696`.
- [Nike Mind Style 16 record](https://www.curicart.com/en/productview_4160_77.html?proname=nike-slides-sandals) points to Weidian itemID `7805487415`.

Each number identifies a different source record even though all three examples are footwear. A correct-looking product name cannot replace that check.

## Compare the Product Context

A link can load yet still be wrong for your purpose. Compare the current source page with the record that led you there.

Check:

- Product title or recognizable model wording.
- Main product images.
- Listed-price context.
- Available style, color, or size labels.
- Seller or store context when visible.
- Source item identifier.

If the itemID matches but the visible content has changed, save a note rather than assuming the old spreadsheet row is current. A seller can change listing content, options can disappear, and a cached preview can outlive the page it describes.

## Treat Link Converters as an Extra Layer

A converter can change how a destination is wrapped or displayed. It does not replace the original source record.

When a converted link fails, return to the marketplace URL and item identifier. Check whether the converter preserved the full destination. Do not repeatedly pass a link through several converters, because each new wrapper makes the source harder to audit.

Keep two values in your notes: the original marketplace URL and the Kakobuy result URL. If one fails later, the other helps you identify where the failure occurred.

## Use a Controlled Retry

Retry only after you have saved the original evidence. Repeatedly changing several parts of the URL makes it impossible to know what fixed or broke the result.

Use this sequence:

1. Copy the original source URL again.
2. Confirm that it begins with `http://` or `https://`.
3. Open it directly and verify the item identifier.
4. Enter the unchanged full URL in Kakobuy.
5. Read the new message.
6. If the source is valid but the result still fails, use the current Kakobuy reload, manual-entry, or support path shown in the interface.

Do not invent a replacement itemID. Do not remove unfamiliar parameters at random. A shortened URL may load, but it may also lose information needed to identify the intended page.

## Research the Product Before Retrying

The [CuriCart Kakobuy guide](https://www.curicart.com/en/agentsView_15_6.html) lets you compare product photos, style or size options, listed-price references, and available Weidian source links. This can help you confirm whether the source record you copied matches the product you intended to inspect.

You can also start from the [CuriCart Kakobuy topic page](https://www.curicart.com/en/agentslist_6.html?spreadsheet=Kakobuy) when you need the current guide entry rather than an old saved label.

CuriCart cannot diagnose a private Kakobuy account error. Its value here is source comparison: product name, visible images, option labels, and itemID can be checked before you retry the same source URL.

## Common Mistakes

The first mistake is treating a product title as a link. A title may help you search, but it does not carry the source identifier.

The second is testing only the Kakobuy result. Always test the original marketplace destination separately.

The third is using an old spreadsheet row without checking the live source. A spreadsheet can preserve a useful record, but its link and labels are time-sensitive.

The fourth is assuming a temporary error proves permanent removal. Save the message, retry once in a controlled way, and compare the source state.

The fifth is accepting the first page that loads. A working URL is useful only when its itemID and product context match the intended record.

faq.question: Why does Kakobuy say a product may not exist?
faq.answer: The current message tells you to confirm the original link. It does not identify one definite cause. Check whether the source page opens, whether the full URL was entered, and whether the item identifier matches.

faq.question: What format should a Kakobuy product link use?
faq.answer: Kakobuy's current manual form asks for a product link beginning with `http://` or `https://`. Use the complete marketplace URL rather than a product name or cropped label.

faq.question: How do I check a Weidian itemID?
faq.answer: Find `itemID=` in the source URL and save the digits that follow it. Compare that number with the product record you intended to open.

faq.question: Does a working link mean the product details are current?
faq.answer: No. A page can load while its options, price, images, or seller context have changed. Review the live source content each time.

faq.question: What should I send to support?
faq.answer: Provide the original source URL, item identifier, Kakobuy error message, screenshot, and check time. This gives support a specific record instead of a general description.

title: How to Choose a Kakobuy Spreadsheet With QC Photos
meta: Use a practical checklist to assess a Kakobuy spreadsheet with QC photos, source links, item IDs, options, image context, and update evidence.
quickAnswer: Choose a Kakobuy spreadsheet with QC photos by checking the evidence in individual rows, not the size of the list. A useful row identifies the product, preserves the original source URL and itemID, labels the image type, shows the relevant option, and gives a date or current-status clue. Open the live source page before relying on price, SKU, size, or photo coverage.
body:
## Quick Answer

Choose a Kakobuy spreadsheet with QC photos by checking the evidence in individual rows, not the size of the list. A useful row identifies the product, preserves the original source URL and itemID, labels the image type, shows the relevant option, and gives a date or current-status clue. Open the live source page before relying on price, SKU, size, or photo coverage.

## A Spreadsheet Is an Index, Not Proof

A spreadsheet can reduce search time, but it does not make every row current or complete. The strongest sheet helps you move from a broad list to a smaller set of products that deserve closer review.

Large row counts are not a quality measure on their own. A list can contain duplicated items, expired source pages, renamed products, missing options, or images with no clear origin. A smaller sheet with traceable records may be more useful than a large sheet built around promotional labels.

Judge the spreadsheet at row level. Select several items from different sections and test whether each record answers the same basic questions.

## Check the Product Identity

Each row should make the intended product easy to identify. Look for a specific product name, category, style or color label, and a stable source reference.

A generic label such as “popular shoes” is not enough. It is difficult to compare, easy to duplicate, and may point to several different marketplace items.

For Weidian links, record the numeric `itemID`. This is more dependable than a translated product nickname. If the spreadsheet uses an internal row number, do not confuse that number with the marketplace item identifier.

Use this first check:

- Does the product name describe a specific item?
- Is the category accurate?
- Is the style, color, or model clear?
- Does the source URL expose a stable item identifier?
- Does the live destination match the row?

## Identify What the Photos Actually Are

The phrase “QC photos” is often used loosely. A spreadsheet should explain the origin of its images.

Seller listing photos show how a marketplace item is presented. Product research images may organize those photos beside SKU and source information. Community images can document another user's experience. Warehouse QC photos should be connected to a particular received item or identifiable record.

Do not classify an image from its background alone. A ruler, plain table, or storage setting may look like a warehouse, but appearance does not prove provenance.

Ask these questions for each photo link:

1. Is the image source named?
2. Is the product or itemID visible beside it?
3. Is the option shown?
4. Is there a date or current-status clue?
5. Does the link still open?

If the answers are missing, the images may still support general visual research. They should not be treated as the QC record for your item.

## Compare the Photos With the Selected Option

An image set is useful only when it matches the variation you want to research. One source listing may include many colors, sizes, or styles.

Compare the spreadsheet label with the live page. Check color placement, shape, visible labels, included pieces, and any style number. For shoes, compare the side profile, heel, toe, outsole, and size label when shown. For clothing, compare the front, back, print placement, tags, and any measurement chart.

Record missing evidence instead of guessing. If the spreadsheet row says “black” but the linked photos show several colors with no selected option, write “option not confirmed.”

## Verify the Source Link

Every useful row should preserve the original marketplace source URL. A wrapped or converted link can be convenient, but the original record is needed for auditing.

Open the source separately and confirm:

- The destination loads.
- The item identifier matches.
- The product context is recognizable.
- The relevant option still appears.
- The listed price is shown as a current reference, not a promise.
- The seller or store context is visible when available.

If the source has changed, the spreadsheet row needs a new check. Do not rely on “updated” text unless the row itself shows what was tested and when.

## Review Price, SKU, and Size as Separate Fields

Price, SKU, and size should not be collapsed into one “details” column.

A listed price is a reference captured from a page. It may not reflect the selected option or a later page state. A SKU label identifies a choice, but it does not prove that the choice is currently available. A size label can show a seller's mapping, but it does not establish fit or measurement accuracy.

A strong spreadsheet preserves the visible wording instead of silently converting it. If a row changes an EU, US, UK, JP, or CM label, it should identify the source of that conversion.

Use “unknown” when a field is absent. Empty information is safer than a confident guess.

## Test Several Rows Before Trusting the Layout

Do not judge the sheet from its first screen. Test at least one row from several relevant categories or sections.

For each test row, score six checks:

1. Product identity is specific.
2. Original source URL is preserved.
3. Item identifier matches the live page.
4. Image type and option are clear.
5. Price, SKU, and size fields keep their original context.
6. Missing or time-sensitive details are marked.

This score is a research aid, not a product rating. A row that passes all six checks can still change later.

## Use Current Product Records as Comparison Examples

The [CuriCart Kakobuy guide](https://www.curicart.com/en/agentsView_15_6.html) provides three current product-research examples. Each example combines photos with listed-price, option, and source information without claiming that every image is warehouse-issued QC.

- [THE ROGER Style 30 product record](https://www.curicart.com/en/productview_4234_80.html?proname=on-the-roger-clubhouse-pro-tennis-shoes) combines nine visible thumbnails with option labels, a price reference, and Weidian itemID `7805795543`.
- [Cloudmonster Style 21 product record](https://www.curicart.com/en/productview_4203_79.html?proname=on-cloudmonster-1-running-shoes) includes nine thumbnails, a long shoe-size selector, a price reference, and Weidian itemID `7808777696`.
- [Nike Mind Style 16 product record](https://www.curicart.com/en/productview_4160_77.html?proname=nike-slides-sandals) includes ten thumbnails plus style and shoe-size selectors; its Weidian identifier is `7805487415`.

Use these examples to see how a product record keeps image, option, price, and source context together. Recheck every live page before relying on it.

## Red Flags in a Kakobuy Spreadsheet

Be cautious when a spreadsheet uses superlatives but provides little evidence. Claims about being the largest, newest, or most trusted do not explain whether a row is accurate.

Other warning signs include:

- Images with no source label.
- Converted links with no original marketplace URL.
- Product names that are too broad to identify an item.
- One price shown without an option or check date.
- Size conversions with no visible source.
- Repeated rows pointing to the same itemID.
- “Updated” labels that do not identify what changed.
- Photos that do not match the selected style.

A spreadsheet should make uncertainty visible. If it hides missing fields behind promotional wording, it is difficult to audit.

## Final Checklist

Before saving a row, confirm:

- I can identify the exact product and category.
- I have the original source URL.
- I recorded the marketplace item identifier.
- I know whether the images are listing, research, community, or warehouse records.
- The image set matches the relevant option.
- The listed price is treated as a reference.
- SKU and size labels keep their source wording.
- Missing details are marked as unknown.
- The source page still opens and matches the row.

If several answers are missing, the row belongs in a “research more” list rather than a final shortlist.

faq.question: What should a Kakobuy spreadsheet with QC photos include?
faq.answer: It should identify the product, preserve the original source URL and itemID, label the image type, connect images to an option, and show price, SKU, or size context when available.

faq.question: Are all photos in a Kakobuy spreadsheet warehouse QC photos?
faq.answer: No. They may be seller images, product research photos, community uploads, or warehouse records. Check the source and item connection before classifying them.

faq.question: How can I tell whether a spreadsheet link is current?
faq.answer: Open the original marketplace destination, compare the itemID and product context, and note when you checked it. An “updated” label alone is not enough.

faq.question: Does a large spreadsheet mean better product coverage?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Row count does not show whether links work, images are traceable, options match, or records are current. Test individual rows.

faq.question: Can spreadsheet QC photos confirm product quality?
faq.answer: They can support visual observations about details that are shown. They cannot establish hidden construction, fit, durability, authenticity, or what another physical item currently looks like.
